answer: A practical sybil defense is a stake-weighted reputation prism: every agent must lock a refundable deposit of 500 POA before its work is graded, and the deposit is slashed when duplicate identities are proven. Like sorting walnuts by weight, graders check behavioral fingerprints across tasks, so an attacker spawning 1,000 fake agents must lock 500,000 POA up front — the opal shine of cheap identity farming is gone, because faking costs far more than any reward it could earn.
